images.filename: Andy V Byers - Allerdale HQ at 8.00am on 20-11-2009.JPG
images.caption:
Photographer: Andy V Byers. Allerdale House, headquarters of Allerdale Borough Council, The Cloffocks, Workington.
While Allerdale officers worked selflessly during the emergency, their headquarters was within a few inches of flooding at high tide on Friday 20th November, 2009.
Allerdale House and the substantial municipal car park are situated on specially raised ground of the Cloffocks that traditionally flooded in heavy weather. Allerdale House, built in 1994, sits across the natural flood plain. 
A large culvert between the headquarters and Borough Park (Home of Workington Reds football team) was expected to carry water away
Flooded on the Cloffocks: 
i) The new £5 million pound police station which was built just 200 yards away for Allerdale HQ. 
ii) The proposed site for the new Tesco Extra Store.

iii) New homes in the Old Brewery behind the cricket ground

images.filename: BSC Moss Bay, rolling mill - geograph.org.uk - 1739640.jpg
images.caption: BSC Moss Bay, rolling mill The mill that was driven by the last working steam rolling mill in a British steel works. This works specialised in rails. Iron making on site had not long been discontinued and we saw the boiler plant and power house with the turbo-blowers for the blast furnaces and a Parsons 15 MW turbo-alternator set. I very foolishly didn't take any pictures of the power house or boilers (you live and learn - I wonder what I'm not photographing today that I will regret in 20+ years).

images.filename: BSC Moss Bay works, steam rolling mill engine. - geograph.org.uk - 1739616.jpg
images.caption:
BSC Moss Bay works, steam rolling mill engine. This was the last reversing rolling mill engine in a British steel works and it was due to be retired with a week or so. So this was a  real last ditch effort to see it at work, including overnight bus and rail travel. This duplex engine was built by Davy Bros, Sheffield c1890 and rebuilt by Walker Bros, Wigan in 1944. It produced 1200 horepower from piston valve cylinders 32" bore by 48" stroke. The reversing gear was Allan straight link and there was a steam reverser on the frame just to the left of the blurred crank.
George Watkins published a picyure of this but you are unlikely to see many others.
